html:
SMTO-HTTP-0014 — SMTO couldn't find the file to send to the web service

GUID: 042307d2-37be-42d2-9458-664acca24a08
Slug: http-context-unavailable
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to send a file to a web service, but that file isn't available in this conversation. Nothing was uploaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Add the file to this conversation with Add files to conversation in the message box, then ask SMTO to upload it. SMTO can only upload files that have been added to the same conversation.
  2. If you added the file in a different conversation or replaced it since, add the current copy here too instead of referring to the old one. Files are shared per conversation, and an old reference may no longer point to a usable file.
  3. Make sure the files for one upload add up to 8 MB or less; for larger files, ask SMTO to upload them in separate requests. An upload over 8 MB is currently reported with this same message.

What success looks like

  • SMTO uploads the file and shows the service's reply instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the file storage for conversations may not be set up. Don't paste the file's contents into the chat if it holds private information.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An HTTP upload or retained-response operation could not proceed because no scoped context store is available or the referenced context_id is not granted to this conversation.

What this means

  • An upload/retained-response operation lacks the scoped context store, or a context reference cannot be bound/read under the current grant. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • An upload/retained-response operation lacks the scoped context store, or a context reference cannot be bound/read under the current grant.

How to diagnose it

  • Check current conversation ownership, context grant and stored artifact availability without substituting arbitrary filesystem paths.

How to fix it

  • skills/http/files.py raises this when the execution context has neither native_receipts nor native_state_db_path, or ContextStore.bind rejects the context_id for this conversation scope; because HttpValidationError is a ValueError, an upload over the 8 MiB budget is currently also reported here. Configure the native state store, re-grant the file to the current conversation and pass its exact ctx_ id.
  • Restore the scoped context store or reselect the authorized current artifact reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended context reference binds in this task and bounded file access succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
